summary: Joe Cribb is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of London (Queen Mary). He served at the British Museum (1970–2010), Hebei Normal University (2021), and the Ashmolean Museum.
Joey Hung works in Buddhist studies and other fields. After attending schools including the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, Hung held a post at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Jogendra Singh is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Presidency College, Chennai, and Bangabasi College. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (from 1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog works on Buddhist, Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies. Educated at UC Berkeley and Indiana University, he held posts at UC Santa Barbara (1997–1998) and Southern Methodist University (around 2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) was an Indologist, Buddhologist, and linguist. Educated at Utrecht and Leiden (doctorate under Antonie Rutgers), he taught at Maastricht (1858–1862), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865), and held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist who held posts at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later held academic posts at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a German linguist educated at the Wilhelmsgymnasium. He held posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano, the Bavarian Cadet Corps, the Bavarian State Library (1829), and the University of Munich (1828, 1846).

Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held academic posts at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1807–1819), Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) was a linguist educated at Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He served at the Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and as chief librarian at the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787).
Johann Elias Schlegel (1719–1749) was an 18th-century scholar who was educated at Schulpforta (~1733–1739) and Leipzig University (~1739–1743).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840) studied at Ernestinum Gotha, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen. He spent his academic career holding a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1776 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart (1776–1841) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797) and subsequently held an academic post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1809).

Johann Friedrich Pfaff (1765–1825) studied at Karlsschule Stuttgart and the University of Göttingen. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Helmstedt (1788–1810) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1810–1825).

Johann Gildemeister (1812–1890) was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, Christian Lassen, and A. W. Schlegel. He later served as professor at Marburg (~1845–1859) and Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn (1752–1827) was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1775) and the University of Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten (1792–1860) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Greifswald and under Silvestre de Sacy. He held professorial posts at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and the University of Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850).

Johann Gottfried von Herder (1744–1803) studied at Königsberg under Immanuel Kant. He held positions at Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, the Court of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach as General Superintendent (1776), and served as director of Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium (~1776–1803).

Johann Gustav Stickel (1805–1896) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena and under Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at Jena (1830–1836).
